review_notes: I read the whole file. The only new definition is `HasPotentialGoodReduction`. A search of Mathlib for "PotentialGoodReduction" and "potential good reduction" found nothing. Mathlib's Reduction file has `HasGoodReduction` and the minimal-model API, and the new definition builds on those instead of replacing them. A search of the repo shows the Tate-module file uses this definition; I found no second definition of it. The remaining declarations are theorems: the `iff` unfolding lemma, `intro`, the smul invariance lemma, the j-invariant criteria, and the Legendre and Deuring good-reduction lemmas. Rubric exclusions rule these out as standalone theorem duplication or proof-shortening candidates. `hasPotentialGoodReduction_iff` is `Iff.rfl`, but it is a theorem and not a competing concept. I did not examine `TauCeti.FiniteDVRExtension` or `IsLocalization.IsInteger` beyond how this file uses them. Neither is defined here. I found no concept in this file that is an avoidable competitor to an existing Mathlib one.
